facts.statement: The genus Corythosaurus was described by Barnum Brown in 1914.
facts.quote: authority: Brown, 1914

facts.statement: Corythosaurus was estimated to be 7.7 to 9 meters long with a skull and crest 70.8 cm tall.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus has an estimated length of 7.7 - 9 m and has a skull, including the crest, that is 70.8 cm tall.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest of Corythosaurus was likely used for vocalization.
facts.quote: The most likely function of the crest is thought to be vocalization.

facts.statement: A Corythosaurus specimen was preserved with its last meal, consisting of conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits, found in its chest cavity.
facts.quote: One Corythosaurus specimen has even been preserved with its last meal in its chest cavity.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 5240 was discovered in 1911 and secured in the fall of 1912 by Barnum Brown in Alberta.
facts.quote: The first specimen, AMNH 5240, was discovered in 1911 by Barnum Brown in Red Deer River of Alberta and secured by him in the Fall of 1912.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Corythosaurus was found in the Belly River Group.
facts.quote: The specimen came from the Belly River Group of the province.

facts.statement: The discovery of the holotype included impressions of much of the creature's skin.
facts.quote: As well as an almost complete skeleton, the find was notable because impressions of much of the creature's skin had also survived.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown published a detailed description of Corythosaurus in 1916 based on specimen AMNH 5338, which serves as the plesiotype.
facts.quote: In 1916, the original author, Brown, published a more detailed description that was also based on AMNH 5338, which is therefore the plesiotype.

facts.statement: Two well-preserved specimens found by Charles H. Sternberg in 1912 were lost in 1916 when the SS Mount Temple was sunk during World War I.
facts.quote: The two best preserved specimens of Corythosaurus, found by Charles H. Sternberg in 1912, were lost on December 6, 1916, while being carried by the SS Mount Temple to the United Kingdom during World War I.

facts.statement: A 2009 study supported separating C. intermedius from C. casuarius based on their different times in the Campanian and non-identical features.
facts.quote: C. intermedius lived at a slightly later time in the Campanian than C. casuarius and the two species are not identical, which supported the separation of them in a 2009 study.

facts.statement: Benson et al. (2012) estimated the average length of Corythosaurus to be 9 meters.
facts.quote: Benson et al. (2012) estimated that Corythosaurus has an average length of 9 m.

facts.statement: Testing of a model concluded that the average weight of Corythosaurus was 3.82 tons.
facts.quote: After testing, it was concluded that the average weight of Corythosaurus was 3.82 t.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul (2016) estimated C. casuarius reached 8 meters long and 2.8 metric tons, while C. intermedius reached 7.7 meters long and 2.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated that C. casuarius reached 8 m long and 2.8 MT in weight and that C. intermedius reached 7.7 m in length and 2.5 MT in weight.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is classified as a lambeosaurine, related to Lambeosaurus, Nipponosaurus, Velafrons, Hypacrosaurus, and Olorotitan.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus is now thought to be a lambeosaurine, thus related to Lambeosaurus, Nipponosaurus, Velafrons, Hypacrosaurus, and Olorotitan.

facts.statement: The skull of Corythosaurus, including its crest, is estimated to be 70.8 cm tall.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus has an estimated length of 7.7 - 9 m and has a skull, including the crest, that is 70.8 cm tall.

facts.statement: The name Corythosaurus means "helmeted lizard" and is derived from the Greek word for "Corinthian helmet".
facts.quote: The generic name Corythosaurus is derived from the Greek κόρυθος,(korythos), "Corinthian helmet", and means "helmeted lizard".

facts.statement: Proportionally, the skull of Corythosaurus is shorter and smaller than those of Edmontosaurus, Kritosaurus, or Saurolophus.
facts.quote: Proportionally, the skull is much shorter and smaller than that of Edmontosaurus (formerly Trachodon), Kritosaurus, or Saurolophus.

facts.statement: When including its crest, the superficial area of the Corythosaurus skull is almost as large as that of other hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: But, when including its crest, its superficial area is almost as large.

facts.statement: More than twenty skulls of Corythosaurus have been discovered.
facts.quote: Over twenty skulls have been found from this dinosaur.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus possessed a tall, elaborate bony crest on its skull containing long air passages.
facts.quote: The animal bore a tall, elaborate, bony crest atop its skull that contained the elongate narial passages.

facts.statement: The crest of Corythosaurus resembles that of a cassowary bird or a Corinthian helmet.
facts.quote: The crests of Corythosaurus resemble that of a cassowary or a Corinthian helmet.

facts.statement: The crest of the type specimen measured 83.7 cm from beak to tip, 81.2 cm in total length, and 70.8 cm in height.
facts.quote: The total length of the crest from the beak to the uppermost tip of the type specimen is 83.7 cm, its total length is 81.2 cm, and its height is 70.8 cm.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of the holotype was 66.9 cm long and 10 cm deep.
facts.quote: The lower jaw of the holotype is 66.9 cm long and 10 cm deep.

facts.statement: The sides and tail of the holotype were covered in various types of scales.
facts.quote: In the holotype of C. casuarius, the sides and tail are covered in scales of several types.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is one of the few hadrosaurids with preserved skin impressions on its hind limbs and feet.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus is one of very few hadrosaurids which have preserved skin impressions on the hind limbs and feet.

facts.statement: Although once thought to be semi-aquatic due to webbed feet, the 'webs' were actually deflated padding similar to modern mammals.
facts.quote: It was once thought that this dinosaur lived mostly in the water, due to the appearance of webbed hands and feet. However, it was later discovered that the so-called "webs" were in fact deflated padding, much like that found on many modern mammals.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown identified specific characteristics in 1914 to distinguish Corythosaurus from other Alberta hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: A set of characters were indicated by Barnum Brown in 1914 to distinguish Corythosaurus from all other hadrosaurids from Alberta.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown expanded the list of distinguishing features for Corythosaurus in 1916.
facts.quote: In 1916, Brown expanded the character set to include even more features.

facts.statement: It is debated regarding the exact structure of the crest, as Barnum Brown incorrectly identified the praemaxillae as nasals.
facts.quote: Brown assumed that they extended from the beaks' tip to the highest spot along the crest and that, unlike those in other genera, the nasals meet in the center and are not separated in front by an ascending premaxillary process. However, Brown mistook the praemaxillae for the nasals.

facts.statement: Many presumed traits of the snout described by Brown are incorrect due to confusion between bone types.
facts.quote: Again, the presumed traits of the snout are incorrect because Brown confused the praemaxillae with the nasal bones and the nasal bones with the frontals.

facts.statement: Many postcranial traits once thought unique to Corythosaurus are now known to be shared with other lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Most of the postcranial traits are today known to be shared with various other lambeosaurines.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is classified as a hadrosaurid dinosaur within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus is currently classified as a hadrosaurid in the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is closely related to other hadrosaurs including Hypacrosaurus, Lambeosaurus, and Olorotitan.
facts.quote: It is related to other hadrosaurs such as Hypacrosaurus, Lambeosaurus, and Olorotitan.

facts.statement: Research by Benson et al. in 2012 grouped Corythosaurus with Velafrons, Nipponosaurus, and Hypacrosaurus as fan-crested lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Benson et al. (2012) found that Corythosaurus was closely related to Velafrons, Nipponosaurus, and Hypacrosaurus, with them forming a group of fan-crested lambeosaurines.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Corythosaurus may have been cathemeral, active in short intervals throughout the day.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Corythosaurus and modern reptiles suggest that it may have been cathemeral, meaning it was most active throughout the day at short intervals.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus likely possessed a sensitive middle ear, indicated by a thin stapes and large eardrum.
facts.quote: The presence of a thin stapes (an ear bone that is rod-like in reptiles), combined with a large eardrum, implies the existence of a sensitive middle ear.

facts.statement: Scientists speculate Corythosaurus could produce loud, low-pitched calls resembling a trombone or wind instrument.
facts.quote: Scientists speculate that Corythosaurus could make loud, low pitched cries "like a wind or brass instrument", such as a trombone.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus emitted low-frequency sounds through its nasal passages when exhaling.
facts.quote: The nasal passages emit low-frequency sounds when Corythosaurus exhaled.

facts.statement: Crested hadrosaurs were once incorrectly thought to be aquatic due to what was mistaken for webbing but is actually padding.
facts.quote: When they were first described, crested hadrosaurs were thought to be aquatic, an assessment based incorrectly on webbing that is now known to be padding.

facts.statement: It is proven that Corythosaurus crests lacked holes and could not function for buoyancy, as water pressure at 3 meters would prevent lung inflation.
facts.quote: However, it has now been proven that the crest did not have any holes in the end and the water pressure at even 3 m would be too great for the lungs to be able to inflate.

facts.statement: Benson et al. (2012) concluded Corythosaurus fed on soft vegetation due to its shallow and delicate beak.
facts.quote: Benson et al. (2012) realized that the beak of Corythosaurus was shallow and delicate, concluding that it must have been used to feed upon soft vegetation.

facts.statement: A preserved Corythosaurus specimen contained conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits in its chest cavity, indicating it was a browser.
facts.quote: A Corythosaurus specimen has been preserved with its last meal in its chest cavity. Inside the cavity were remains of conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits, meaning that Corythosaurus probably fed on all of these, implying that it was a browser.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus casuarius is one of the few lambeosaurines with surviving fossilized juveniles assigned to the species.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus casuarius is one of a few lambeosaurines, along with Lambeosaurus lambei, Hypacrosaurus stebingeri, and H. altispinus, to have had surviving fossilized juveniles assigned to it.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus began developing its crest at half adult size, whereas Parasaurolophus juveniles started growing crests at only 25% of adult length.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus started developing its crest when they were half the size of adults, but Parasaurolophus juveniles grew crests when they were only 25% as long as adults.

facts.statement: Young and adult Corythosaurus differ from Parasaurolophus by having sinuous skull sutures rather than smooth, straight ones.
facts.quote: Young and adult Corythosaurus are similar to Lambeosaurus and Hypacrosaurus, but dissimilar to Parasaurolophus in that the sutures of the skull are sinuous, not smooth and straight.

facts.statement: Over fifty articulated specimens from many genera have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: In the Dinosaur Park Formation, over fifty articulated specimens have been found that come from many different genera.

facts.statement: Earlier paleontologists recognized four genera and thirteen species in the Dinosaur Park Formation based on size and crest shape differences, a classification now largely revised.
facts.quote: Earlier, four genera and thirteen species were recognized from the formation's area when paleontologists used differences in size and crest shape to differentiate taxa.

facts.statement: Fossils of Corythosaurus have been found in the Oldman and Dinosaur Park Formations in Canada.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the upper Oldman Formation and lower Dinosaur Park Formation of Canada.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus lived approximately 77 to 75.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus lived from ~77–75.7 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found as a carcass that had floated onto a beach, surrounded by water-worn bones and shells.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was clearly a carcass that had floated up on a beach, as Unio shells, water-worn bones, and a baenid turtle were preserved all around it.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus likely lived in woodland forests and may have occasionally wandered into swampy areas.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus probably lived in a woodland forest and might have occasionally wandered into swampy areas.

facts.statement: Studies suggest Corythosaurus and its contemporaries occupied slightly different ecological niches to avoid direct competition for food.
facts.quote: Studies of the jaw anatomy and mechanics of these dinosaurs suggests they probably all occupied slightly different ecological niches in order to avoid direct competition for food in such a crowded eco-space.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the crest functioned for vocalization, acting like a trombone to amplify sound waves as the animal exhaled.
facts.quote: La función más probable de la cresta es la vocalización. Como en un trombón, las ondas de sonido viajarían a través de muchas cámaras en la cresta, y luego se amplificarían cuando el Corythosaurus exhalara.

facts.statement: A preserved specimen contained conifer needles, seeds, branches, and fruits in its thoracic cavity, indicating its diet.
facts.quote: Un espécimen de Corythosaurus se ha conservado con su última comida en su cavidad torácica. Dentro de la cavidad había restos de agujas de coníferas, semillas, ramas y frutos.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus had an estimated length of 9 meters and a skull with crest height of 70.8 centimeters.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus tiene una longitud estimada de 9 metros, y tiene un cráneo, incluida la cresta, que mide 70,8 centímetros de alto.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is known for having high crests that resemble those of a cassowary or a Corinthian helmet.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus es conocido por muchos cráneos con altas crestas. Las crestas se asemejan a las crestas del casuario o a un casco corintio.

facts.statement: The nearly complete holotype specimen of Corythosaurus was discovered by Barnum Brown in 1911.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus se conoce de muchos especímenes completos, incluido el holotipo casi completo encontrado por Barnum Brown en 1911.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton is missing the tail tip and part of the forelimbs but preserves impressions of polygonal scales.
facts.quote: Al esqueleto holotipo solo falta la última sección de la cola y parte de las extremidades anteriores, pero se conservó con impresiones de escamas poligonales.

facts.statement: The genus Corythosaurus was named by Brown in 1914.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1914

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Corythosaurus is Corythosaurus casuarius.
facts.quote: type_species: Corythosaurus casuarius

facts.statement: Corythosaurus is classified within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Corythosaurus belongs to the tribe Corythosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Corythosaurini

facts.statement: Corythosaurus intermedius was described by Parks in 1923.
facts.quote: subdivision: Corythosaurus intermedius Parks, 1923

facts.statement: Corythosaurus excavatus, described by Gilmore in 1923, is a synonym of Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Corythosaurus excavatusGilmore, 1923

facts.statement: Recent research suggests Olorotitan is a close relative of Corythosaurus, despite not sharing the crest shape.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la investigación reciente ha sugerido que Olorotitan es un pariente cercano de Corythosaurus, aun sin compartir la forma de la cresta.

facts.statement: Thomas M. Lehman observed that Corythosaurus has only been found in southern Alberta despite being abundant in the region.
facts.quote: Thomas M. Lehman has observed that Corythosaurus hasn't been discovered outside of southern Alberta, even though it is one of the most abundant Judithian dinosaurs in the region.

facts.statement: Large Late Cretaceous hadrosaurs in North America had remarkably small geographic ranges despite their size and mobility.
facts.quote: Large herbivores like the hadrosaurs living in North America during the Late Cretaceous had "remarkably small geographic ranges" despite their large body size and high mobility.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated in 2012 that Corythosaurus had an average length of 9 meters.
facts.quote: Benson et al. en 2012 estimaron que Corythosaurus tiene una longitud promedio de 9 metros.

facts.statement: Estimates published in 2001 place Corythosaurus among the largest hadrosaurids, smaller only than Shantungosaurus and Parasaurolophus.
facts.quote: Estimaciones de tallas más recientes de Corythosaurus, publicadas en 2001, encuentran que el género está entre los hadrosáuridos más grandes, solo más pequeños que Shantungosaurus y Parasaurolophus.

facts.statement: The total length of the Corythosaurus specimen AMNH 5240 was 8.1 meters with a weight of 3.0785 tonnes.
facts.quote: La longitud total del espécimen de Corythosaurus AMNH 5240 fue de 8.1 metros, con un peso de 3,0785 toneladas.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus was a gregarious herbivore that fed on low plants and forest fruits.
facts.quote: Corythosaurus era un herbívoro que presentaba un comportamiento gregario y se alimentaban de plantas bajas y frutos de los bosques.

facts.statement: Corythosaurus had a toothless beak but possessed hundreds of small teeth in its jaw that were constantly replaced.
facts.quote: Su pico no tenía dientes, pero sí la mandíbula, en la que había cientos de pequeños y eran reemplazados constantemente a medida que caían.

facts.statement: More than 20 skulls of Corythosaurus have been discovered.
facts.quote: Más de 20 cráneos se han encontrado de este dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Like other lambeosaurines, Corythosaurus possessed a high, elaborate bony crest on its skull containing elongated nasal passages.
facts.quote: Como con otros lambeosáuridos, este animal tenía una cresta ósea alta, elaborada encima de su cráneo, que contenía canales nasales alargados.

facts.statement: The nasal passages extended through the crest into separate side pockets, a central chamber, and forward into the respiratory system.
facts.quote: Los canales nasales se extendieron en la cresta, primero en los bolsillos separados en los lados, luego en un solo compartimiento central y hacia adelante en el sistema respiratorio.

facts.statement: Scientists speculate that Corythosaurus could produce sounds like low moans or a brass instrument.
facts.quote: Los científicos especulan que Corythosaurus podría hacer un sonido "como gritos graves como el un viento o un instrumento de latón".

facts.statement: When herds of different genera mixed, the crest likely helped attract mates and the keen sense of smell helped individuals return to their group.
facts.quote: Cuando manadas de diferentes géneros se mezclaban, su cresta, que posiblemente debe haber servido para atraer hembras y su agudo sentido olfativo debe haberle ayudado a retornar con los suyos.

facts.statement: It was once thought Corythosaurus lived mostly in water due to webbed-looking hands and feet, but the supposed membranes were actually fatty tissue pads similar to modern mammals.
facts.quote: Alguna vez se pensó que este dinosaurio vivió sobre todo en el agua, debido al aspecto de manos y de pies palmeados. Sin embargo, fue descubierto más adelante que las supuestas "membranas" era de hecho almohadillas de tejido liposo, como se encuentran en muchos mamíferos modernos.

facts.statement: The crests of Corythosaurus resemble those of a cassowary or a Corinthian helmet.
facts.quote: Las crestas de Corythosaurus se asemejan a las de un casuario, o un casco corintio.

facts.statement: The two halves of the Corythosaurus crest are separated by a midline suture.
facts.quote: Las dos mitades de la cresta están separadas por una sutura mediana.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of the holotype measures 66.9 centimeters in length and 10 centimeters in depth.
facts.quote: La mandíbula inferior del holotipo mide 66,9 centímetros de largo y 10 centímetros de profundidad.

facts.statement: The total crest length from the beak to the highest point of the holotype is 83.7 centimeters, with a total length of 81.2 centimeters and a height of 70.8 centimeters.
facts.quote: La longitud total de la cresta desde el pico hasta la punta más alta del ejemplar tipo es de 83.7 centímetros, su longitud total es de 81.2 centímetros y una altura de 70.8 centímetros.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown defined Corythosaurus in 1914 by a comparatively short skull with a large helmet-like crest formed by the nasals, prefrontals, and frontals.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown en 1914 para distinguir a Corythosaurus de todos los demás hadrosáuridos de Alberta, un cráneo comparativamente corto con una gran cresta en forma de casco formada por los nasales, los prefrontales y los frontales.

facts.statement: It is debated that some original cranial features were incorrect because Brown confused the premaxillae with nasal bones and nasal bones with frontals.
facts.quote: Los supuestos rasgos del hocico son incorrectos porque Brown confundió los premaxilares con los huesos nasales y los huesos nasales con los frontales.

facts.statement: Brown assumed the nasals extended from the beak tip to the crest's highest point and were central, but he actually confused the premaxillae with the nasals.
facts.quote: Brown supuso que se extendían desde la punta de los picos hasta el punto más alto a lo largo de la cresta y que, a diferencia de otros géneros, las nasales se encuentran en el centro y no están separadas por un proceso premaxilar ascendente. Brown, sin embargo, confundió los premaxilares con los nasales.

facts.statement: Brown incorrectly assumed the frontals covered the entire external surface of the crest's top and rear, when they were actually the nasals.
facts.quote: Brown también pensó que en la parte superior y posterior de la cresta, toda la cara externa está cubierta por los frontales. Otra vez cometió un error, lo que él asumió como los frontales son, de hecho, los nasales.

facts.statement: The nasal fossae end at the rear of the squamosals in a short, hooked process.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales terminan en la parte posterior de los escamosos en un proceso corto y enganchado.

facts.statement: The prefrontals form part of the crest, but Brown confused the lower part of the premaxilla's upper ramus with the prefrontal.
facts.quote: Los prefrontales también forman parte de la cresta, sin embargo, Brown confundió la parte baja de la rama superior del premaxilar con el prefrontal.

facts.statement: The real frontals are largely internal to the base of the crest structure and are not visible from the side.
facts.quote: Los frontales reales, en gran medida internos a la estructura de la base de la cresta, no son visibles desde un lado.

facts.statement: The folds enclose air ducts extending to the front of the snout, ending in narrow openings called "pseudonares" or false nostrils, which Brown confused with real nostrils.
facts.quote: Los pliegues encierran conductos de aire que se extienden por los pasajes nasales hasta el frente del hocico. Allí terminan en aberturas estrechas, a veces llamadas "pseudonarinas", fosas nasales falsas. Brown los confundió con las narices reales o las fosas nasales.

facts.statement: Due to incorrect identification, Brown assumed the holotype's premaxillary process was shorter than in Kritosaurus and Saurolophus and did not touch the lacrimal, but in reality it touches the lacrimal and extends far behind the eye socket.
facts.quote: Debido a su identificación incorrecta, Brown supuso que el proceso inferior del premaxilar del holotipo era más corto que en Kritosaurus y Saurolophus, y que el proceso no se une con la lagrimal, otra diferencia de esos géneros. El praemaxilar en realidad toca al lagrimal y se extiende hacia la parte posterior hasta muy atrás de la cuenca del ojo.

facts.statement: Benson et al. (2012) noted that the Corythosaurus beak was shallow and delicate, concluding it was used to feed on soft vegetation.
facts.quote: Benson et al. en 2012 se dieron cuenta de que el pico de Corythosaurus era poco profundo y delicado, y concluyeron que debe haber sido utilizado para alimentarse de vegetación blanda

facts.statement: Fossilized stomach contents from Corythosaurus include conifer needles, seeds, twigs, and fruits.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Corythosaurus may have been catemeral, active throughout the day in short intervals.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones entre los anillos esclerales de Corythosaurus con las aves y reptiles modernos sugieren que puede haber sido catemeral, es decir activo durante todo el día en intervalos cortos

facts.statement: The presence of a thin stapes and large tympanum implies Corythosaurus had a sensitive middle ear.
facts.quote: La presencia de un estribo delgado, un hueso de la oreja que es similar a una vara en los reptiles, combinado con un tímpano grande implica la existencia de un oído medio sensible

facts.statement: It is debated whether the hearing of hadrosaurids, including Corythosaurus, was highly developed due to an elongated closed cochlear duct limb.
facts.quote: El sentido del oído en hadrosáuridos, específicamente estudiado en Lophorhothon, también parece haber estado muy desarrollado debido a una extremidad del conducto coclear cerrada alargado

facts.statement: Dudgeon, Brown, and Evans (2026) described the internal crest anatomy of mature Corythosaurus individuals.
facts.quote: Dudgeon, Brown & Evans (2026) describe the internal crest anatomy of mature individuals of Corythosaurus casuarius, C. intermedius and Lambeosaurus lambei
